page: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-64 is a memory-optimized server instance designed for memory-intensive workloads. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 976 GB of dedicated RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 15.25 GB per core. The processor includes a 54 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AES cryptography. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the m3-megamem-64 demonstrates strong multi-core and memory-intensive performance. It achieves a strong rating in the Passmark CPU score of 54571.25 and Passmark database operations of 26047.32, indicating high efficiency for relational and in-memory database workloads. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong at 293.92 GB/sec, alongside strong Geekbench multi-core and software compilation scores. Single-core performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1577.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1852.19. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, reaching 150.66 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 62.1 GB/sec for large uncached writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m3-megamem-64 represents a high-resource density profile tailored for enterprise applications that require massive memory footprints without the need for local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it qualitatively cost-effective for large-scale in-memory databases, heavy database operations, and memory-bound data processing tasks. It is well-suited for workloads such as SAP HANA, large-scale Redis deployments, enterprise database management systems, and complex software compilation pipelines.
